# Reactio Draw

Draws structures and reactions with **Reactio Draw** inside Obsidian (desktop only):

0. **The reaction of a reaction note.** The note template has a picture under **Table**: *Click to draw the reaction and the table*. A click on it creates `Files/A_122.cdxml` (the code is the first part of the note name: `A_122 text text` → `A_122`) and opens it in Reactio Draw. Draw the reaction and the reagent table; **Ctrl/Cmd+S**, **Ctrl/Cmd+W** or × saves without a question and closes the tab (the side panels come back). CDX Scheme Image then draws `A_122 scheme.svg` from it and puts it under **Table** in place of the placeholder (as for ChemDraw files). Later a **click on that scheme picture** opens `A_122.cdxml` in Reactio Draw again; closing the tab saves it. The file is ordinary CDXML (ChemDraw and the Reactio Draw app open it) with the full Reactio document in a comment. Notes whose reaction is a ChemDraw `.cdx` are not touched: if `A_122.cdx` exists, the placeholder only reminds you to open it in ChemDraw. While a Reactio tab is open the side panels are hidden; the ones that were open come back when the last Reactio tab closes (setting *Hide side panels while drawing*). To draw reactions in another program instead, set *Open reaction files in* to *Default program outside Obsidian*: the click on the placeholder creates `A_122.cdxml` as a blank sheet and opens it in the program the system uses for `.cdxml` files (ChemDraw, the Reactio Draw app); an existing `A_122.cdx` or `A_122.cdxml` opens as it is, also on a click on its scheme picture; when you save it there, CDX Scheme Image puts the scheme into the note.

1. **Search queries.** The pencil button in the left ribbon (or *Reactio Draw: Open a new drawing*) opens an empty drawing tab. Draw a structure or a reaction and press the **search** button at the top of the tab: the search dialog of *Reaction Structure Search* (1.7 or later) opens with the drawing as the query.
2. **Your own schemes in notes.** Click into a note, then press the **picture** button of the drawing tab: the drawing is saved as `Files/<note> scheme.rdraw` and `![[… scheme.rdraw]]` is inserted at the cursor (`![[… scheme.rdraw|300]]` sets the width). The `.rdraw` file is an SVG picture with the Reactio Draw document inside (`<metadata id="reactio-draw">`); because of its own extension Obsidian does not treat it as an image (no zoom on click): the plugin shows the picture in the note, and **a click on it opens the drawing** in Reactio Draw. **Save** rewrites the file and the picture in every note updates. Renamed to `.svg`, the file opens as a picture in other programs.
3. **CDXML files.** *Save as CDXML* stores the drawing in the `Drawings` folder as CDXML that ChemDraw opens, with the full Reactio Draw document in a comment (`<!--rd:…-->`, the marker Reactio Draw itself uses), so Reactio Draw reads it back with its tables and conditions. *Open a drawing file* opens schemes (`.rdraw`), Reactio Draw documents (`.reactio`, saved back in place), `.cdxml`, `.mol`, `.rxn`, `.sdf` and `.smi` files; a file outside the `Drawings` folder (for example a reaction's ChemDraw file opened as a query) is never overwritten — Save asks for a new name.

A drawing opened from a note (reaction file or `.rdraw` scheme) is saved when its tab is closed; a new drawing is saved only with **Save**; an unsaved drawing shows ● in the tab title. Ctrl/Cmd+W also works while the drawing has the focus (the plugin listens for it through Electron, because the keys go to the drawing frame). The ChemDraw files of reaction notes are **not** opened in Obsidian: they keep opening in ChemDraw or in the Reactio Draw desktop app, and CDX Scheme Image reads them as before. Reaction Structure Search skips folders named `Drawings`.

## Names
3D shapes, 3D rotation, NMR prediction and names → structures are part of Reactio Draw's web version and work in the tab as they are, offline. **Structure from a name** reads common names (*aspirin*, *THF*), systematic names (*2-methylpropan-1-ol*, through OPSIN inside the page), names of natural products and drugs, and CAS numbers. **Name the selected structure** (IUPAC name through openclatura, checked back with OPSIN) needs the installed **Reactio Draw app** (Windows, Mac, Linux) with Python and `pip install openclatura`: the plugin runs the app's command line `reactio op …` without opening its window. The app is found in its usual place (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Reactio Draw\reactio.exe`, `/Applications/Reactio Draw.app/Contents/MacOS/reactio`, `~/.local/bin/reactio`) or set in *Settings → Reactio Draw → Reactio Draw app*; for a name the page does not read, Structure from a name asks the app too. Nothing of the app is copied into the vault.

## How it works
`reactio/reactio.html` is Reactio Draw's web version, unchanged. The plugin shows it in an iframe with `?embed&origin=app://obsidian.md` (Reactio Draw's embedding mode: a blank drawing of its own, no access to the browser's saved documents, answers only the window that embeds it) and sends it commands of its API by `postMessage` (`export`, `set`, `markSaved`, …).

The page is built into `main.js` (Obsidian installs a plugin from the community directory as `main.js`, `manifest.json` and `styles.css` only). When the first drawing tab opens, the plugin writes the page to `reactio/reactio.html` in its own folder if it is missing or differs from the built-in one (after an update of the plugin); a page that is already there and the same is left alone. Nothing is downloaded.

## Network, files and programs
- **Network:** the plugin makes no network requests. Reactio Draw's page goes online only when you press one of two buttons: *Check for updates* asks `api.github.com` for the newest release, and *Search PubChem* (Properties, CAS number) sends the InChIKey of the selected compound to `pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov`. Everything else, including NMR prediction and reading names (the tables and the name reader are part of the page), runs offline on this computer.
- **Files outside the vault:** none are written. The plugin writes Reactio Draw's page into its own folder (`<vault>/.obsidian/plugins/reactio-draw/reactio/`). For names (below) it looks for the Reactio Draw app in its usual install folders or at the path set in the settings.
- **Other programs:** *Name the selected structure* (and *Structure from a name* for a name the page does not read) runs the installed Reactio Draw app's command line (`reactio op …`), and the setting *Open reaction files in: Default program outside Obsidian* opens reaction files in the program your system uses for `.cdxml`. Neither happens unless you use these functions.
- **Accounts and payments:** none.

## Building, tests and updating Reactio Draw
`node build.mjs` bundles `src/` into `main.js` and puts `reactio/reactio.html` into it. The tests are in the plugin's source repository (with the sources and fixtures), not in the vault's plugin folder: `node tests/page.test.js` (the page built into `main.js` and written into the plugin folder when missing or changed), `node tests/bridge.test.js` runs the Reactio Draw page in headless Chromium (Playwright: `NODE_PATH="$(npm root -g)" node tests/bridge.test.js`) and checks every command the wrapper uses on the example files, including that a file opened and saved again keeps its Reactio record and its CDXML (Reactio Draw 1.15 may write where labels sit on the first save); `node tests/bridge-data.test.js` (the drawing kept in CDXML and SVG and read back; the message protocol), `node tests/external.test.js` (the setting *Open reaction files in*, with a mocked Obsidian and Electron), `node tests/shortcut.test.js` (Ctrl/Cmd+S and W on US, Russian, AZERTY, QWERTZ and Greek layouts), `node tests/load.test.js` (`main.js` loads).

A new Reactio Draw release goes in with one command: `node update-reactio.mjs ReactioDraw-Web.zip 0.10.1` takes the page (`Reactio Draw.html` of the zip, or `index.html` of the repository; a folder or the HTML file itself works too) with its licence files into `reactio/`, sets the plugin version in `manifest.json` and `versions.json`, adds a CHANGELOG entry, builds `main.js` and runs the tests that need no browser. The wrapper's code does not change unless Reactio Draw changes its embedding API.
